title: EMBER World Chronology
zh: 月尘 · 黑曜协议 · 纪年表
hook: In 1910 a small family factory makes bandages for a war. A century later its heirs hold the keys to the human mind, and the Moon has become a battlefield.
html:
Dating: A.E. years count from 1959, the year of the first Moon landing (A.E. 000 = 1959). BAE years count backwards before it (BAE.049 = 1910). See AE.014.

The old wars1910–1955

BAE.0491910

Dominic Leighton is born, the fifth child, with four older brothers. His father runs a small factory called Leighton Mechanical Webbing Works, which mainly makes textiles and bandages.
Mr. and Mrs. Leighton had always hoped for a daughter, but Dominic was their last child.

BAE.0461913

To expand sales, the Leightons move to Flower Harbor. Mrs. Leighton goes first with little Dominic; Mr. Leighton and the four sons stay behind to run the factory.

BAE.0451914

An unprecedented great war breaks out on the continent, drawing in almost every country on Euralis.
Leighton Mechanical Webbing Works becomes a military supplier and grows fast. All four sons still at home join the Renus army.

BAE.0401919

The war ends in Renus’s defeat. The Leighton family has amassed sizable starting capital and built up experience as a military supplier. But of the four sons who joined the army, only the fourth survives.

BAE.0291930

Von Bauhner enrolls at the Zumpfen University of Technology.

BAE.0251934

Von Bauhner publishes several papers on liquid-fuel rocket propulsion and spaceflight engines, and quickly drives practical tests of the technology.
Because of the defeat in the previous war, tensions inside Renus grow worse, leading at last to another war frenzy aimed at proving the nation’s racial superiority. The papers are quickly made a banner for that goal, and the Renus authorities begin pouring money into them.

BAE.0221937

A U2-S rocket crosses the Kármán line. Humans send a man-made object into space for the first time.

BAE.0201939

Driven by real conflicts and war fever, war breaks out again.
With painful memories of the last war, the Leighton family sells its holdings in Euralis, moves to the Calpe Federation, and uses the medical resources it has built up to found the .

BAE.0171942

The Piper-3 probe, carried by a U4 rocket, successfully orbits the Moon, takes close-range photographs and sends them back by radio.
In the photographs of the far side, traces of regular man-made structures can be faintly made out. Renus names them the “.”
Spurred by this, the Renus authorities cancel a batch of superweapon programs and start shifting all resources to the Moon-landing project, trying to get “a bargaining chip big enough to win the war” from the Relics. But what that “chip” actually was is described only vaguely in the documents, mostly on the basis of occult guesswork.

BAE.0161943

Piper-5 orbits the Moon and takes more photographs, including the famous far-side Relic photograph “Triangle Pit.”
But this is the Renus regime’s last successful launch. After that, the course of the war forces the space program to be halted.

BAE.0141945

The Allied armies take Zumpfen and end the war. From captured documents, every side obtains material on the Renus Moon program and learns that the Relics exist.
As leading members of the Allies, the Calpe Federation and the Gotias Alliance begin competing hard for the scientists involved in the Renus Moon program, to push forward the secret space race that starts at once.
Anthony Leighton is born, the only son of Dominic Leighton.

BAE.0131946

After a speech by the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom of Britannia, the space race between the two camps led by the Calpe Federation and the Gotias Alliance becomes fully public. Building orbital military power becomes an open top priority for both camps.

BAE.0111948

Leighton Bio sets up the Mir Laboratory internally, focused on exploring cutting-edge fields.

BAE.0091950

The Gotias Alliance photographs the far side of the Moon and sends back a large amount of photo data.
With launch-site building in mind, both camps begin competing to win over low-latitude countries.

BAE.0071952

The Gotias Alliance carries out the first crewed orbital flight.
The same year, a Calpe Federation crewed spacecraft crosses the Kármán line.

BAE.0051954

To serve the space race, both camps begin focused development of their own network systems. The Calpe Federation launches AERIS; the same year the Gotias Alliance launches NEVRA in response.
Over the next few years, to balance their spending, both camps bring more civilian organizations and institutions into their space projects.

BAE.0041955

The Order makes its first pilgrimage around the Moon.
Swept up by the dramatic space race, a branch sect of an ancient monotheistic faith, called the Sharwen Order, grows steadily. They believe the Most High God came from the Moon, and the social climate of the day wins the sect a large following.
The space race’s build-up of technology, along with heavy civilian involvement, makes commercial space travel more and more common. Seizing the chance, the Sharwen Order organizes its first pilgrim group to fly around the Moon. The pilgrimage later becomes an important rite of the Order, held every five years.

The Moon rush1959–1973

AE.0001959

On July 20, the Calpe Federation lands on the Moon in the Sea of Tranquility.
On July 30, the Gotias Alliance lands on the far side of the Moon.
Both sides declare their landing sites “exclusive development zones.” World tension reaches an all-time high, and at one point both sides threaten each other by deploying intermediate-range missiles.
But with restraint on both sides, the situation eases and direct hot war is avoided.
A few months later, both sides jointly announce the discovery of the far-side Relics, and say they will begin scientific and exchange cooperation and develop the Relics together.
This news galvanizes every country able to launch payloads. All of them start trying, with astonishing efficiency, to send landers to the Moon, hoping to win a place in the exploration.
With the official discovery of the Relics, the Sharwen faith’s zeal is fully ignited, and it becomes almost the only orthodox sect of its monotheistic religion.

AE.0011960

The Calpe Federation and the Gotias Alliance begin joint exploration of Relic 0. During it they discover a new, stable superheavy element, , and Relic products that can be activated and run but whose workings can’t be understood. These Relic products are named “,” and various institutions begin analyzing them.
Their earlier fierce rivalry has left both camps facing serious financial crises. Both begin organizing “academic lunar exploration,” letting more civilian bodies onto the Moon and into the Relics to fill the gap.
A crewed capsule launched by the Euralis Space Agency lands on the Moon, and spaceports become the signature landmark of every low-latitude country.
The Sharwen Order makes its second lunar pilgrimage. During it, believers bang on the portholes so fanatically that a porthole works loose and loses pressure, and the ship has to make an emergency return.

AE.0021961

The first lunar expedition made up entirely of civilian organizations lands on the Moon.

AE.0031962

Ivan Sergeyevich Lebedev is born in the Gotias Alliance.
The Leighton Group makes a huge gamble and decides to join the Relic exploration, even though the entry ticket might drain all of the company’s money.
Seventeen-year-old Anthony Leighton takes part in the expedition as an intern. After returning to Earth, he switches his university major from neuroscience to linguistics.
After this, the Leighton Group pushes deeper into Relic exploration, becomes one of the first companies to enter the D2 zone, and at the end of the year sets up a remote exclusive development zone in D2.

AE.0041963

Building on research into the AG-class black boxes found in the Relics, Logheed-Marten launches the first prototype shuttle with an AG engine.
This ion engine, combined with black-box technology, has very high fuel efficiency and excellent thrust. The prototype shows huge potential.

AE.0051964

The Olovin Design Bureau launches the first AX-engine shuttle, based on another black box.

AE.0061965

Both camps’ heavy-lift shuttles enter service, and both sides’ capacity to deliver payloads to orbit rises sharply.
Because of their huge strategic value, the zones producing AG- and AX-type black boxes are tightly controlled by all sides, and this raises tensions again. Over the next few years, more Relic entrances are found and more black-box technology is put to real use, and the lunar land rush reaches its peak.
At the same time, the parties exploring follow different laws, and with no single body to coordinate them, friction between development zones grows by the day. Both camps begin tightening control of launch capacity and steadily expanding their space forces.

AE.0071966

Anthony Leighton graduates and joins the Mir Laboratory, taking up again the neuroscience he had not finished.

AE.0101969

The Mir Laboratory formally unveils the prototype of the , with Anthony Leighton taking part as a researcher.
Within the year, Leighton Technology launches the commercial Obsidian Protocol 1.0 (OPV1). This version can set up a stable brain-machine link and needs no invasive device. At the same time it releases the experimental OPV2 to partner companies and laboratories. This version needs invasive surgery, but in theory allows advanced functions such as memory expansion and assistant programs.
Because the long-term vision of the Obsidian Protocol includes exploring the digitization of human consciousness, many religious groups oppose it.
The Sharwen faith holds a fierce internal debate. Some branches argue that Leighton’s OPV1 and OPV2 are “works of wisdom” and should be supported; others argue that the consciousness upload in Leighton’s vision is a blasphemy against the Most High that cannot be tolerated.

AE.0111970

The Rhaetia Conference: the escalating rivalry deals another heavy blow to every party’s economy, and the nations return to cooperation talks to discuss signing a space treaty. The first conference is held at Rhaetia Base by the leaders of several lunar companies and organizations.

AE.0131972

AERIS and NEVRA are successfully networked together, and the first form of an internet with a camp-intranet / global-public-network structure takes shape.

AE.0141973

With the signing of the first Space Treaty, the is formally founded, and 1959 is formally set as year 1 of the A.E. calendar.
The treaty states that high orbit and the Moon fall under the Lunar Management Committee. Only its member companies and non-governmental bodies may set up development zones there.
On the surface, the great powers now develop high orbit through companies acting as their agents, but in practice they take complete control of high-orbit development rights. Countries that had not clearly picked a side in the Calpe–Gotias rivalry essentially lose their chance to get in.
By promising to sell military-grade Obsidian Protocol to both sides, the Leighton Group wins membership in the Lunar Management Committee.
Over the next few years, the Committee’s members launch the Second Lunar Enclosure, developing the Moon and the Relics on a large scale, and unwritten rules gradually form: “tonnage per unit of time agreements” and “turn a blind eye to far-side conflict.”

The Obsidian age1974–2009

AE.0151974

The Gotias Alliance begins market reforms within its camp.
The process causes some social unrest and leaves the Gotias Alliance clearly weaker for the next decade. It pulls back strategically, but in practice it becomes better at absorbing outside resources.

AE.0161975

As the Lunar Management Committee settles into steady running, the period of joint Calpe–Gotias control formally ends. The member companies jointly set up the High Orbit Security Force (MG) as the armed force for areas under the Committee.
The first public-network stock exchange formally opens.
As a 13th-birthday present for Ivan, an uncle in the Calpe Federation opens an investment account for him and deposits 1,990 kabi in it.

AE.0171976

The Leighton Group launches the first commercial augmentation surgery using the , and with it makes OPV3 public.
If OPV1 and 2 were a first taste, the launch of OPV3 was enough to make people cry out that the future had arrived. Faced with this technology, the definition of consciousness became deeply blurred for the first time, and the definition of a person softened with it.

AE.0181977

The first V-type is obtained. The Coordination Cores’ immense computing power shocks every party, and Zone 633, where it was found, becomes a hotspot. It is later found that V-type and other types of Coordination Core turn up in other zones too.
Because the trade in these black boxes, their appraisal and their handling are so large, their transit station on the Moon gradually grows into a black market. This abandoned supply point lies between the near side and the far side and once supplied Orbit 1, so it is called “Wasserkran” (water crane).

AE.0191978

The first draft of Automated Warfare, built on the Coordination Cores’ computing power, is submitted as a memorandum. The Central Intelligence Affairs Bureau begins a planned increase in its purchases of V-type Coordination Cores.
This draft is the first to propose the radical plan of using Coordination Cores in the war-command system, with every serving soldier augmented with the Obsidian Protocol.

AE.0201979

The Gotias Alliance’s National Security Agency obtains information that the Calpe Federation is preparing for automated warfare. The Gotias army at once begins building, on a large scale, an army based on Coordination Cores.

AE.0211980

The GC-series black boxes are discovered. These black boxes have a “gravity phase” property: an outside power source can change how they are acted on in a gravity field. Combined with other systems, they make the first anti-gravity engine, the “gravity sail,” possible.
Because this means another leap in delivery capacity, its strategic importance is enormous, and both sides at once tighten control of the zones that produce it.

AE.0221981

Ivan, who has made a little money on the stock market, makes a bet with his university roommate. He writes a self-optimizing investment algorithm that starts from “betting completely at random,” registers a capital company for it with 100 kabi of starting money, and bets that within a year it will earn more than his friend.
With a sense of humor, Ivan names this mini-company Midas Capital.

AE.0231982

The first anti-gravity ship prototype makes its test flight, and the gravity sail becomes a hot research field.
Ivan wins the bet. After that, he often tinkers with Midas’s investment model as a hobby.

AE.0251984

Rhaetia Base builds the largest bonded warehouse on the Moon and becomes the preferred delivery point for Ying futures.

AE.0261985

In the shadow of the arms race, both the space fleets of the Earth nations and the company fleets of Lunar Management Committee members begin to be built up on a large scale.
At the same time, the lift capacity of anti-gravity ships makes it possible to build large space stations.

AE.0281987

The Rhaetia Base expansion plan, under pressure from the Lunar Management Committee, gradually leans toward a design centered on the large mass driver “.”

AE.0311990

The Fars War: the Calpe army uses an automated warfare system as its general staff for the first time and deploys units. It is the first large-scale use of OPV4 soldiers on Earth.
The war creates huge numbers of refugees. The Sharwen faith takes in many believers who strongly resent OPV4, and rejection of Leighton and the Obsidian Protocol becomes the mainstream view within the faith.
Victory in the Fars War shows the enormous potential of automated warfare. Meanwhile, as the carving-up of the Relic zones nears its end, friction between the parties rises again.
As a prelude to hot war, every camp begins an early war of public opinion, and begins systematically controlling and even falsifying all kinds of information. In time this leads to the data crisis known as “History Failure.”
Ivan enlists. Before leaving, he gives Midas one last upgrade, installing a small Coordination Core in its local hardware.
The core instruction of this upgrade is: “I want to make everyone rich.”

AE.0371996

Ivan goes missing in the war.

AE.0401999

Through information manipulation and other means, Midas assembles a complete enough shadow board, takes over all of Ivan’s assets, and uses money from years of independent investing to buy up and restructure several small companies that are members of the Lunar Management Committee, thereby winning a seat on the Committee.

AE.0412000

The Calpe Federation and the Gotias Alliance each launch their own large-scale space transport plans, and use them to make the world’s countries, especially low-latitude ones, pick sides again.
Under pressure from the two hegemons, almost every country on Earth joins one of the two camps.
As Sleipnir City is built in Sinus Medii, the lunar-faction companies that have quietly drifted out of Earth’s control, especially the more independent ones, begin cooperating politically in greater depth.
Sleipnir sits in the Rhaetia crater, and the whole city has grown up around the giant mass driver. It has every kind of facility, and is full of docks, factories and large transport hubs, giving efficient links between shuttles, lunar transport craft, lunar highways and railways.
Because most early lunar builders had high augmentation rates, Sleipnir City has no single sealed structure. Most buildings keep their air in with their own airlocks. As more natural humans and less-augmented residents moved in, the lunar builders sealed several small ring mountains around Sleipnir City and turned them into airtight satellite towns, which together with Sleipnir form the largest metropolitan area on the Moon.
Because Earth’s currencies keep wobbling, the Moon’s mining companies are the first to settle large deals among themselves in Ying, sidestepping the swings of Earth’s multipolar currency system.
Before the tenth lunar pilgrimage, the Sharwen faith holds a great sermon blaming the unrest since the Fars War on agitation by “non-human” groups. At the same time, the sermon shows more acceptance of partly cyborg and partly cyberbrained people, reflecting the faith’s further secularization in this period.

AE.0472006

The Lunar Merchants’ Association is founded in Sleipnir and proposes building a lunar network system on a brand-new public network, to make Lunar Management Committee member companies more efficient.

AE.0502009

Building on research into Coordination Cores, Lauren, a young scholar at the Masatuck Institute of Technology, proposes the concept known as “”: by having a Coordination Core take full charge of allocating society’s resources, steer humanity’s group beliefs in return, and so build a truly perfect society.

RDL

The Great War2010–2040

AE.0512010

Amid endless friction, hot war between the two camps finally breaks out and quickly turns into the worldwide “.” Both sides deploy complete automated warfare systems:
Every level of these armies thinks about war in a distributed way. Once war begins, they pursue their war aims through a distributed, self-adapting structure.
The basic units allocate all the war resources in their own system to serve this aim.
Even when the original command structure is broken up, military units regroup and act according to the set aim. When scattered units meet up again, they swap information to update the battlefield picture and correct their tactics.
At the very start of the war, along with the first round of nuclear strikes, both sides also attack each other’s space assets. The chain reaction forms a vast debris cloud above the Earth.

AE.0522011

The debris cloud reaches critical density, and almost every craft in orbit is destroyed.
The unfinished skyhook systems are destroyed too.
Getting through the debris cloud by any means other than heavily armored anti-gravity ships is almost never successful, and people all but lose the ability to reach or leave high orbit.

AE.0532012

At the Lunar Merchants’ Association’s urging, the Lunar Management Committee and all its members declare a full ceasefire within their territory, with the MG in charge of security in the region.
All shares previously held by Earth governments are frozen.
Some Earth space forces outside the debris cloud try to seize, by force, Committee ships that had belonged to their own side, and exchange fire with Committee forces.

AE.0552014

The “Turbulence” working group is formally set up, focused on developing a new generation of production-coordination systems.

AE.0562015

The High Orbit Joint Declaration is published, proclaiming the founding of an independent polity, the .
The High Orbit Union’s basic unit is still the company. Companies get council seats according to their size, and votes are run by a rotating board. Disputes between companies are settled by the High Union Court under an improved international law; inside a company, the company largely governs itself.
Most of the Earth governments’ previously frozen assets are gradually returned to the companies, and some are confiscated by the High Union to offset war reparations.
At the same time, the High Union Central Bank is founded and issues the High Union coin, requiring all Ying metal trades to be settled in it.
Without Earth’s support or interference, companies with strong forces or key resources grow ever more powerful, and the first forms of factions appear around them. At first they form loose council alliances to push or block proposals together. Later they take stakes in each other or merge, binding ever closer. Friction between factions sometimes happens, but on the whole every side cares more about building a complete industrial system and ending its dependence on Earth’s resources.

AE.0582017

The Agricultural Merchants’ Association is founded:
Although the OPV4 share of the population is far higher than on the ground, most of the High Union’s population is still not OPV4. Most companies producing food and cash crops are family cooperative farms on colony satellites or deep in lunar cities, and their members have low augmentation rates.
But because these companies are each small, and because “Lunar Supremacism” and “Augmentation Superiority” are on the rise inside the High Union, these companies, which in fact “feed the High Union,” are slowly pushed to the margins. Disappointed farm owners gradually come together as the Agricultural Merchants’ Association, to push their demands with one voice.

AE.0592018

“Turbulence” is experimentally connected to three closely cooperating deep-space mining companies. It takes over primary control of most of their facilities and allocates their means of production through internal planning. The experiment runs for a year and goes well. The three companies begin taking stakes in each other and start pushing the “Advanced Mining League” plan.

AE.0602019

During the Great War, Midas completes several key acquisitions and expands fast.

AE.0612020

As space debris keeps falling, travel between the Earth and the Moon gradually gets easier, and lightly protected shuttles can get through the debris cloud.
Before this, only OPV4 augmented people or a lucky few could ride heavy ships into the High Union. Now, with more traffic, the High Union sees its first wave of refugees.
This wave includes huge numbers of natural humans, many of them Sharwen believers. Because they are less augmented, they tend to gather on farming and residential colony satellites, in practice filling the High Union’s shortage of farming population. But at the same time, the tension between augmented and natural humans keeps growing.

AE.0622021

Seeing a business opportunity, Theseus Biotech is the first to partner with finance companies and launch low-interest prosthetic loans. Residents can borrow against their future income to get OPV4 augmentation surgery. They also busily prepare to offer this service on Earth.

AE.0632022

The Saturn-8 Incident:
The conflict between augmented and natural humans comes into the open inside the High Union, and the first area that openly shuts out OPV4 augmented people appears. The management company of the farming colony satellite “Saturn-8” is the first to declare that, from the end of that year, all OPV4 augmented people in the satellite will be considered not to have full human rights.
Because people at OPV2 and above make up a large share of the High Union, this discriminatory law angers many companies, and they protest one after another.
In response, a “Full Human Rights Bill,” jointly proposed by sixteen companies, is submitted to the High Union, demanding that the law clearly state that OPV4 people have full human rights within the High Union and are protected by the High Union Council.
But, unexpectedly, many member companies of the Agricultural Merchants’ Association declare support for the Saturn-8 resolution, and the bill fails.
And before the second submission, the media report widely on possible deep ties between the sixteen companies behind the bill and Theseus Biotech, and the slogan “Beware Augmentation Supremacism” spreads fast.
And as the Advanced Mining League grows more active, word spreads that the League will become an even tighter alliance, and many fear a future of “humans manipulated by non-humans” or “small companies manipulated by big companies.” The Agricultural Merchants’ Association’s support for Saturn-8 escalates further into a defense of “corporate territorial autonomy” under the High Orbit Joint Declaration.
In the end the “Full Human Rights Bill” is rejected again, the Agricultural Merchants’ Association’s cause is further framed as “a victory for free will,” and the media dub them the “.”

GoF
AE.0642023

The Advanced Mining League formally proposes the “” plan, which aims to build an alliance of companies working closely together and deeply linked through their control systems. Inside, the companies use “the Guide,” a product of the Turbulence project, for unified allocation, chasing the highest development efficiency.
In the wake of the “Full Human Rights Bill” affair, many people criticize the proposal as “an evil plan to enslave humans with machines.” But the Mining League’s member companies have plainly developed fast over the past five years, so many companies still announce that they will join or become observers.

RDL
AE.0652024

The Reconstruction Development League is formally founded, and preliminary work on connecting the Guide system begins at the same time.

RDL
AE.0682027

Although the Guide project’s chief engineer dies in an accident, the preliminary work is finished successfully, and formal trial running begins.
The former deputy chief engineer, Annie, takes over as chief engineer.

RDL
AE.0712030

“The Guide” begins to take over the running of the Reconstruction Development League in full.
Several companies led by Red Dot Technology and Midas Capital announce a joint project fund to clear geosynchronous orbit and build a new satellite network, extending the High Union’s orbital internet down to the Earth’s surface.
The project is named the “.”

RDLUN
AE.0722031

Led by Saturn-8, many former Agricultural Merchants’ Association companies and a large number of cooperatives announce the formal founding of a joint union, the “Guardians of Freedom,” and announce the “Humanist Parliament” plan: to achieve full internal “complete democratization” through “compound plenary voting.” The Guardians of Freedom declare that their goal is to build a “New Athens.”
The Great War sinks into stalemate and a quagmire, and loss of control over the war keys becomes ever more common. Earth’s nations, now fighting on several fronts at once against both “the enemy” and “their former allied armies,” ask the High Union for help.
The three great factions, now taking shape, all begin sending more aid missions to Earth. They usually give priority to protecting key production facilities and heavy assets, build safe zones around them, then cooperate with local governments and widen their own local influence.
High Union aid eases political relations between the two sides and does help end the war sooner. Through the aid effort, the High Union builds a glowing image of “progress, development, facing the future,” which makes the Earth nations still struggling on through the war look all the more outdated.

GoF
AE.0732032

The Guardians of Freedom formally set up a dedicated ground operations force, the “Longship,” and establish safe zones in several key areas.
Their offensive operations mark a shift in the High Union’s model of aid.

GoF
AE.0742033

The United Network and the Reconstruction Development League also set up their own ground operations forces, and that year successfully establish several safe zones, protecting many key facilities.
To organize larger offensives, the High Union begins forming joint forces under unified MG command.

RDLUN
AE.0752034

The High Union, as a joint army, carries out a large-scale operation called “Operation Flare” and successfully sets up a safe zone deep at the front.
In this operation, the High Union first encounters “the Retainers”: some settled humans do not believe that the war core running their area has “lost control.” However it’s explained to them, they firmly trust their area’s war core and refuse to let the joint army take over.

AE.0762035

The Humanist Parliament gradually takes shape and enters its second stage:
The “Teller” system, which helps count votes quickly, is connected for trial running. Within the year it rules on more than 100,000 disputes and runs well.
The Guardians of Freedom set up a rotating inspectorate. Each group of inspectors is ten randomly chosen citizens. While serving, a citizen can inspect, check and call up every voting record, to make sure the Teller system is reliable.
The Humanist Parliament’s right to vote and right to inspect are both basic human rights. Except in traditional “exclusion zones” such as Saturn-8, OPV4s within most Guardians of Freedom members still have these rights.

GoF
AE.0772036

The United Network’s member companies grow to over 300, and it starts promoting the “Natural Legal Person” scheme. This lets a natural human register all their assets, including their body and their consciousness itself, as registered capital after valuation, and become a company entity. It declares that anyone with dreams of starting a business is welcome to join the United Network.
The same year the scheme passes with limits: a natural legal person counts as a special company, cannot hold a council seat alone, and must attach to an existing High Union company. Even so, the number of United Network member “companies” soars past 500,000. Because valuations in this period are very loose, almost every natural legal person gets a very handsome sum of start-up money.

UN
AE.0782037

The United Network’s satellite network “Monsoon” goes into open trial running, and two large OPV living matrices are built: “Midgard,” which every OPV user can reach remotely by direct connection, and “Alfheim,” for OPV4 people only. The first is a cloud world hosted on distributed servers, reachable from anywhere with a physical connection: a typical public network space. The second is a large data center on the outskirts of Sleipnir City, housing great numbers of OPV4 terminals. The United Network has built a dedicated network space for the consciousnesses in these terminals, with very generous computing power and hardware support, so that every user can have a high-quality, almost all-powerful private domain.
At the same time, the United Network buys great numbers of unactivated OPV4 terminals and stores them in Alfheim itself. An applicant only needs to buy one remotely to jump straight into it. OPV living matrices like this are usually company-owned and built for a set purpose. Alfheim, which the United Network spent a fortune building, is the largest and best-equipped commercial living matrix ever made.
At the end of the year, both systems open to Earth. Among the many OPV users, especially OPV4s, it sets off a new rush to join the High Union by applying online, and the workload of the High Union Immigration Bureau soars.
In the past, getting to the High Union meant boarding an anti-gravity ship, so migration from Earth to the High Union was always limited by lift capacity. Now more and more natural humans on Earth are choosing the digital migration program offered by Theseus Medical:
First, they mortgage their own consciousness to get a prosthetic loan and convert to OPV4. Then they buy an Alfheim terminal and, once there, apply to be an employee of a United Network subsidiary. Theseus Medical immediately transfers the debt, and these migrants can begin applying for High Union citizenship as company employees. These applicants usually join Earth-development companies. Every day they jump into a work body on Earth to do their job, and after work they jump back to their “home” in Alfheim to rest.
As the Great War nears its end, many professional soldiers leave the army. With dire finances and chaotic logistics, many cyborg soldiers are disarmed and discharged on the spot. These people, ravaged by war and left with poorly maintained military cyborg bodies, find remote migration to the High Union an obviously good option, and this makes the United Network’s armed strength grow fast.

UN
AE.0792038

The Reconstruction Development League and the Guardians also follow with digital migration programs of their own. Both are far smaller than the United Network’s and can’t offer facilities as good as Alfheim, but they still attract many OPV4 migrants.
At the same time, every side extends its rights and interests within its protected areas on the ground and buys up assets in bulk. The move of “first buy up the assets, then step in to protect those assets” becomes more and more common.

RDLUNGoF
AE.0812040

Brokered by the High Union, the parties on Earth declare a ceasefire. The two great military alliances, led by the Gotias Alliance and the Calpe Federation, are fully dissolved, and the war is over, at least in law.
The High Union sets up many more aid zones and safe zones on Earth. Many people on Earth move into safe zones for better living conditions and security. Some safe zones also start being run under the internal rules of the companies they belong to, so their residents become High Union population in practice.
Using the safe zones as a springboard, more people migrate to the Moon, but this sharpens the tension between migrants and the High Union’s original residents.
Because the High Union’s and Earth’s populations are made up so differently, “Augmentation Superiority” is clearly more widespread inside the High Union. Among Earth people, natural humans’ hostility toward the deeply augmented, especially OPV4s, keeps growing, and thirty years of Great War have left traditional religions facing more doubt.
Against this background, the Sharwen faith, which preaches “humanity above all; God gave humans consciousness to explore the world,” becomes the largest religion in the world. Its Feiwen school, which favors reconciliation and sees OPV4 users as “the lost,” becomes the mainstream.

After the ceasefire2042–2080

AE.0832042

A report: tracking statistics on large numbers of discharged soldiers and digital migrants find some troubling signs —
Among the veterans who have been through countless deaths in brutal ground warfare, some show signs of functional decline such as memory loss, to varying degrees. In extreme cases, some individuals have already lost function entirely.
These OPV4 soldiers really have not died. But they are only alive.

AE.0842043

The United Network’s satellite network “Monsoon” achieves coverage of 50% of the Earth, but orbit clearance is going more slowly than expected.

UN
AE.0882047

The three great factions set up a joint protected area in Spring Lake City, which comes to be called the “City of Three Capitals” and quickly becomes the High Union’s model city on the ground.

AE.0912050

The Demi Case: an extreme augmentation supremacist and OPV4 augmented person, Demi Anderson, maliciously kills four natural humans in Guardians of Freedom territory and then turns himself in to the police. At his trial Anderson shows no remorse whatsoever, and arrogantly claims that “as a superman, I cannot be killed.”
His execution is held up several times, and at one point there are reports that Anderson has escaped. The authorities finally announce that Anderson’s death has been confirmed, but Guardians of Freedom members’ revulsion at OPV4 reaches an all-time high.

GoF
AE.0922051

The police explain the Anderson case and the problems with the execution to the public in detail, but for the public the explanation comes too late, and it even deepens their distrust.
In the end this sparks the largest anti-OPV4 movement ever, across all Guardian territory. Angry natural humans launch a Supreme Referendum of the Humanist Parliament, demanding an anti-OPV4 law like Saturn-8’s across all Guardian territory, stripping every “artificial person” of the vote.
The Supreme Vote is held at the end of December and passes with over 76% support: from 00:00 on January 1, 2053, Earth Standard Time, all OPV4 people within Guardians of Freedom territory lose the right to vote.
The event is officially called the “9th Supreme Referendum” or the “9th Amendment.” But because many Guardian residents openly call OPV4 users “fake people” after it, the event is also often called the “Fake People Act” or the “Fake People Vote.”

GoF
AE.0932052

With the 9th Amendment in force, several companies, including the Odin Group, announce they are leaving the Guardians of Freedom, and the OPV4 share of the Guardians of Freedom’s population falls further.
But after the 9th Amendment, the Teller’s counting delay drops by 60%, which gives the member companies still inside the Guardians of Freedom great confidence.

GoF
AE.0942053

The High Union’s internal power structure gradually stabilizes into a three-way balance.
The boundaries of each power’s territory in the D1 and D2 layers of the Relics gradually reach equilibrium too. The number of open conflicts falls, and the Moon enters a relatively peaceful period of development.

AE.0972056

The Albion Incident.

AE.1052064

Operation Vitusia:
The launch an all-out offensive on the safe zones in former Calpe territory.
Earlier reconnaissance had not detected so huge a force, so the defending troops stationed there are completely unprepared and soon lose all ability to resist.
Though short of heavy weapons and combat experience, the local guard units still manage to organize several lines of defense. Fighting as they fall back, they keep harrying the Rogue Core forces to slow their advance, and at the cost of heavy casualties they cover the escape of large numbers of refugees to the Safe Zone – Dezhnev.
After High Union forces and Earth reinforcements arrive, the front is stabilized again.

AE.1062065

Operation Boomerang.

AE.1142073

The Sapphire Conflict breaks out. It shows that, for the first time since AE.094, a new round of fighting over controlled zones in the Relics is beginning. The conflict gradually escalates, and core companies of some camps start expanding their controlled zones directly.

AE.1162075

The Coldbridge Technology executive defection: Watchtower Defense takes over Coldbridge’s Wild Duck squad entirely.
After this, Coldbridge Technology becomes a subsidiary of Watchtower Defense, and in AE.119 it sells all of its controlled-zone development rights.

AE.1212080

Signal 99676 is discovered. This anomalous gravitational signal is believed to be a rare self-activating black box. The Warthog is sent to recover it.
The Mariner, after picking up this information, is also sent out to intercept the Warthog.
Noticing that both have set out, the Anderson also chooses to head secretly for the area of Signal 99676.

title: Relics and Black Boxes
hook: A probe photographs the far side of the Moon and sees something that was built. Humanity goes inside, and starts taking things apart.
html:
In ’42 the probe Piper-3 made humanity’s first flight around the Moon, photographing the far side and sending the pictures back. The ground received only about 30% of the planned photographs, but scientists could still use them to identify and name features on the far side. In the process, a clearly visible regular structure appeared on the far side, and it was judged very likely to be artificial.

The Renus authorities classified the discovery top secret and poured in resources, hoping that contact with an alien civilization would turn the losing war around.

As the war neared its end, the Aerospace Ministry’s test site fell, and both the Calpe Federation and the Gotias Alliance learned about the Moon program. Both hunted down and courted the former Renus scientists hard. After the war, as the two camps drifted into opposition, both quietly made space exploration and orbital military power their top priorities.

In the early ’60s tensions eased, and the two sides set up space cooperation and explored together. The artificial structures beneath the lunar surface were finally made public and named the “.” The structure Piper-3 had found turned out to be part of an artificial cave, poking up through the surface. The cave was later named “Relic 0,” and it was the first target explored by the joint expedition.

As exploration went deeper, people slowly built up a hazy picture of the Relics:

  • Who built the Relics is unknown. They lack clear indoor and outdoor structures, so there is no easy way to infer what the builders’ bodies were like.
  • Most of each Relic lies below the lunar surface. Its function is hard to infer, and it grows more complex the deeper you go.
  • Building the Relics took very advanced technology. Some materials came from the Moon, but the and Ying-alloy structures used in large amounts very likely came from somewhere else.
  • Most Relics are made up of several open spaces and passages. The former are usually called “domes” and the latter “corridors.” Some domes have unusual radiation, magnetic and even gravitational effects.

The appearance of the Relics shook the whole human world. But the Relic products that could actually be studied were even more fascinating.

From here on, breaking the reactor is about as easy as smashing the chief's head in with a water pipe. The hard part is telling which one you are doing.

Stephen Vinge, Lunar Management Committee

Analysis of Relic products went step by step. It started with photographs and samples. Along the way we saw all kinds of strange materials, some baffling craftsmanship, and physical properties beyond imagination.

Next, people began trying to take apart and analyze the things that were obviously mechanical components. No doubt these structures and devices had their own original functions. But we could not find the Relics’ owners, nor any writing or symbols, so scientists could only test these Relic products with methods close to primitive.

As testing went on, people were delighted to find that some devices could be activated. Many of them, though, were in a state of “can be activated, but cannot be taken apart.” One example is the “GX-type ”: these devices can change how they are acted on in a gravity field when driven by a pulsed power supply, and they became the core component of the “gravity sail.”

Likewise, there are other products whose structure can hardly be called a “device,” but which have remarkable physical properties and can be used directly. One example is the S80, known as the “ribs.” They appear in groups in some areas and seem to be some kind of long, thin vane or frame. Their composition is complex, yet their microstructure is very regular and their mechanical properties are superb. Fitted with shock absorbers, they were used directly as mech weapons.

These Relic products that can be used but not understood are known collectively as “black boxes.”

Research on the Relics and Relic products soon developed its own methods and spawned a string of new disciplines: Relic surveying, which explores and records the Relics’ internal structure; Relic taxonomy, which classifies Relic products; and the most closely watched, Relic engineering, which seemed to bring new progress every day. The basic sciences were in a more complicated position. On one hand, many black boxes smashed the edifice of science humanity had built over thousands of years, as if it were a child’s sandcastle on the beach. On the other hand, many black boxes gave experimental science powerful backing in one leap, and the most ambitious young scientists were getting ready to rewrite every theory since the Renaissance.

Different groups also disagreed sharply about the whole field. The conservative view held that the top priority was to finish surveying the Relics and do everything possible to make contact with their original owners. After all, the “Forerunners” might not be easy to talk to, especially when faced with savages who barge into their yard without a word and start taking things apart and borrowing them. The radical view held that precisely because the original owners were unpredictable and could turn up at any moment, we needed to try every possible way to understand them and to arm ourselves. And many politicians took a far more practical view: rather than worrying about “Forerunners” who might not even be there anymore, first make sure your fist is bigger than your neighbor’s.

The most widely quoted description of the Relics and black boxes is Stephen Vinge’s: “We are like a band of apemen who have just learned to make tools, and have stumbled by sheer luck upon an aircraft carrier stranded in the jungle.” But few people know the worried second half of the quote from this chief scientist of the : “From here on, breaking the reactor is about as easy as smashing the chief’s head in with a water pipe. The hard part is telling which one you are doing.”

  • 锳, “Ying.” An invented element (the 钅 metal radical + 英). The timeline calls it a “stable superheavy element” found in Relic 0. No official English found; “Ying” is its reading.
  • GX-type black box. The timeline calls the gravity-sail black boxes the “GC series.” Both labels are as printed.

  • The closing joke. Breaking the reactor (an accident) and clubbing the chief (using it as a weapon) are equally easy for the apemen. The hard part is knowing which of the two you are actually doing.

title: The Obsidian Protocol
hook: A young intern walks into a forgotten Relic and comes back changed. Within twenty years, anyone can leave their body behind.
html:
When we talk about “Leighton” today, we usually mean Anthony Leighton, born in ’45, who took part in Leighton Industries’ Moon landing operation as an intern in ’62.

The elder Leighton’s investment in the Moon landing was a huge gamble. Nearly everyone else exploring the at the time was a top-tier technology or industrial company. A biotech company with no deep roots, getting by on nothing but enthusiasm, looked badly out of place among them. Of course, from where we stand today, the gamble clearly paid off, with two unexpected results.

The first: inside Relic 79, which nobody else cared about, they found the first consciousness-field response. The young people of the Mir Laboratory saw at once that this could be a key clue, so they followed the trail deeper into the Relic. They had no purpose-built equipment, so the process was close to mysticism. The scientists bounced around the dark Relic like fools, poking about and trying to find their “feeling.” To outsiders (and to some of their own number), these pseudo-scientists had no idea what they were looking for and were simply wasting stamina and supplies, which is to say money.

Luckily, before the budget ran out completely, they did pin down the final “hunting ground.” What exactly they found there is still argued over today, and nobody can say for sure. Either way, that part of the Relic is now the absolute core of the ’s controlled zone, and the birthplace of the .

The second result: Anthony Leighton, equally shaken by the phenomenon, returned to Earth and put his study of neuroscience on hold. He switched to linguistics instead, and after graduating in ’66 he formally joined the Mir Laboratory to work on the Relic project.

Throughout university, Anthony often worked with the Mir studio. He recruited several heavyweight linguists for the lab, and he is said to have played a key part in developing the Obsidian Protocol himself.

In ’69 the Mir Laboratory produced the prototype of the Obsidian Protocol. It was a set of technical protocols for connecting brain information with digital devices. A device using it could read the brain’s signals clearly and send information in a specific format into the brain. At the prototype stage it only let the user produce and receive text and simple graphics through a remote device. In theory, though, the system could let users run far more complex data streams.

Whether it was money pressure or a race to get in first, Leighton Technology could not wait. That same year it launched the commercial version, Obsidian Protocol 1.0 (OPV1). This version could already set up a stable brain-machine link without any invasive device, and it quickly became the hottest platform among hardware developers.

As with the OPV devices sold later (and many Relic products), Leighton sold sealed components directly, along with products that used them (such as the “Contact” series). Both could be used with a dedicated SDK. Leighton claimed that OPV1 was tuned Relic technology and very stable, and that the sealing was added by hand for safety.

That same year they also released the experimental OPV2, offered only to partner companies and laboratories. Unlike OPV1, this version needed invasive surgery, but in theory it allowed advanced functions such as memory expansion and running assistant programs. The long-term vision of the Obsidian Protocol included exploring the digitization of human consciousness, so many religious groups opposed it. Among them, the faith had a fierce internal debate. Some branches stressed that Leighton’s OPV1 and OPV2 were “works of wisdom,” and “the works of wisdom glorify the Most High,” so they should be supported. Others stressed that the consciousness upload in Leighton’s vision was a clumsy imitation of the “Divine Light” and could not be tolerated. The long debate eventually petered out with no conclusion.

Over the next ten years, devices using OPV1 and OPV2 swept the whole market. The best-known was the “Contact” series. This was a personal terminal that combined a communicator with a miniature personal computer. The basic set was a handset plus an OPV1 linker. Used together, they let you control the handset with your thoughts, call up its functions at any time, and in some settings connect straight to the network. The implanted OPV2 linker was made into a separate series, “Vista.” The name came from the fact that first-time users were usually stunned by the sharp, precise UI in their field of view. Vista’s powerful data-stream functions let users run far more complex programs and feel like superhumans.

Contact and Vista earned Leighton vast capital and turned the Leighton Group into a super-giant almost overnight. Meanwhile, as Vista rolled out, Leighton Medical spread everywhere. Nearly every large city had a Leighton Medical branch. These branches handled Vista sales, implanting and maintenance. More importantly, they set the rules and procedures for third parties buying and running OPV devices, and they became the backbone for the roll-out of the next OPV generation.

In ’76 Leighton Medical carried out the first commercial operation using OPV3. The patient was a 45-year-old musician whose sense of touch and hearing had been damaged by a stroke. Leighton’s New Domon Hospital performed a operation to rebuild the damaged areas of his brain. The operation was a success: it fully repaired his damaged brain, and he left the hospital after two weeks of observation. At his routine maintenance a year later, Leighton Medical also gave him a piece of experimental software that let him record and export his musical ideas at any time. Once he got used to it, he could compose whole pieces in his head. The musician lived until the broke out.

Over the next few years OPV3 spread rapidly through medicine and came to be seen almost as a cure-all. As the threshold and limits for its use kept dropping, nobody could say which treatment was the first “unnecessary” OPV3 installation. And once that threshold was crossed, healthy volunteers naturally appeared.

In ’79 the first purely voluntary Theseus Process patient appeared. He was a chess player who simply wanted to digitize part of his brain to gain an edge in calculation. After the operation, the International Chess Federation quickly ruled his attempts to compete illegal (top-level competitions then banned devices such as Contact and Vista). He soon changed direction, though, and made a fortune at unofficial poker games.

The Obsidian Protocol’s impact on the social order kept the whole of the ’70s unsteady. Young people were becoming open to choosing augmentation and implants. Among adults, the split in attitudes this brought was even harder to measure. Countless people poured out their grievances on early regional internet forums: augmented people taking their jobs; a doctor suggesting “you may as well get augmented while you’re here” for a minor illness; coming home after two days of overtime to find their daughter’s eyes glowing with LED light… and so on. Yet compared with the coming , all this was only a prelude.

In ’86 OPV4 and the were made public for the first time, and human society was shaken. OPV4 formally meant that humans could discard their native brain entirely and accept a split between consciousness and body. A consciousness compiled through OPV4 could be stored in a dedicated device, and several “backup” stores could be named. The consciousness could “jump” directly into any store that could be activated. The transfer method was never fully disclosed, but Leighton claimed it used neutrino communication, so it happened at light speed and was very hard to block. Deep-space workers with OPV4 could “rest at home and work in space.”

Humanists worried that it would bring endless life, that the meaning of life would dissolve, and that nothing could hold back nihilism anymore.

Pragmatists worried that as virtual spaces got better, the real world would stop mattering, and human civilization would end in decadence.

Far more people simply doubted it. Many feared that the extracted “consciousness” was only an illusion, a program’s clumsy imitation of the living.

The will is sacred, down with Obsidian.

Sharwen chant

And there were all kinds of conspiracy theories, such as that Leighton had been listening to everyone’s brainwaves through the Contact series all along, and was now ready to take over the world.

Whatever the public reaction, cyborgs using OPV4 soon showed huge advantages in harsh working environments such as spaceflight and the deep sea. So, unlike OPV3’s slow shift from pure medicine to voluntary enhancement, healthy recipients made up a large share of OPV4 users from the start. At the same time, prosthetic loans boomed. Many people took out loans to get cyborg surgery for scarce jobs, then flooded into the OPV3 and OPV4 positions. Scarce jobs stopped being scarce, and desperate cyborgs began to appear among the unemployed, a nightmare for law enforcement.

OPV4’s most important customer was without doubt the military. It is believed that well before ’82, possibly as early as the start of the ’70s (the was founded in ’73, and Leighton Technology was one of the first private bodies to get a “ticket”), Leighton may already have been in contact with the military departments of both great alliances, supplying OPV4 in exchange for the group’s interests on the lunar surface.

When the regional hot war broke out in ’91, the world saw OPV4 cyborg soldiers and “automated warfare” for the first time. Perhaps warnings that “the demon has been let out of the bottle” had grown stale. Public debate focused more on the rights of OPV4 soldiers. By comparison, the Sharwen faith, spreading fast among the refugees and chanting “The will is sacred, down with Obsidian,” looked old-fashioned and rigid. Everyone knew this era had arrived and that more change was coming.

But Anthony and Leighton Technology slowed down.

From the ’90s until the Great War, the Leighton Group kept pushing its space development plans. Once the Great War began, it turned to humanitarian relief. It worked closely with non-profits such as the International Library Federation and did outstanding work protecting the products of civilization.

After the was founded in ’15, the Leighton Group kept a sizable number of seats in it, yet it usually played the mediator on major issues. It even seemed to keep the High Orbit Union at arm’s length.

On some questions of augmented people’s human rights, the Leighton Group was not radical at all, and even seemed somewhat conservative. In the Saturn-8 Incident of ’22, for example, Leighton’s spokespeople never voiced support for either side, and the group simply abstained in the vote. Many believe that in this affair Leighton, the sole supplier of OPV, appeared to step off the stage “of its own accord.” But because it did nothing positive, it in fact stood on the side of the .

Whenever a key High Orbit Union project ran into trouble, it could almost always count on Leighton’s support. When the Complexity Research Center was first being planned, Annie visited Leighton’s research center and got help from several advisers. When Midas Capital was clearing the debris cloud, the Leighton Group lent it several ships at a low price. The Humanist Parliament’s base model was built with support from Titius College at Leighton University.

Toward the end of the war, Leighton kept cutting the cost of using the OPV system and pushed hard on OPV infrastructure. A huge supply of cheap augmentation clearly helped post-war rebuilding, and cheap, widespread OPV4 made large-scale digital migration possible. When the built “Midgard” and “Alfheim,” the Leighton Group sent people from the Mir Laboratory to give them technical support, and that solution became the basis for every large-scale living matrix that followed.

Supporters of the Leighton Group’s actions in the new century usually say that “Anthony is a dreamer who wants to drive civilization forward through technology.” The radicals among them even believe that the discovery of the “Loss of Control” and the brokering of the ceasefire were also the Leighton Group’s great work, and that the High Orbit Union was an ark Anthony built in advance to save human civilization from destruction. Opponents’ views reek of conspiracy theory: Leighton started the war to get more people using OPV; every OPV user will eventually lose their mind and become a slave of the Leighton Group; perhaps our world is already a sham, all of it an illusion made by the Leighton Group.

Anthony is a dreamer who wants to drive civilization forward through technology.

Leighton's supporters

As for the Obsidian Protocol itself, some guess that OPV5 exists and can copy and edit a consciousness. Some even believe OPV6 exists too, but that this technology, which “can blend and split consciousnesses,” is too dangerous, so Leighton quietly hid it. OPV7, supposedly, could create a mind from nothing. None of these claims has any evidence behind it, and even the version numbering is imagined. They are best treated as urban legends. What exactly was found in Relic 79, and what research goes on there, is still the Leighton Group’s most closely guarded secret.

leighton: The Leighton family's company, built on medicine. It bet everything on exploring the Relics, and went on to make the Obsidian Protocol.
